title: Finite etale model from boundary source neighbourhoods and codimension-two extension
statement:
Let $B$ be a Noetherian regular integral domain and let $0\ne f\in B$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme]. Put $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/f]\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $C$ be a finite $B$-algebra and $N=\operatorname{Spec}C$, with its finite structural map $q:N\to X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Suppose $N\times_X U\to U$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose also that for each height-one prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ containing $f$, and each point $z\in N$ above $\mathfrak q$, there is an open neighbourhood $O_z\subseteq N$ such that $O_z\to X$ is etale. Here height one means $\mathfrak q\ne(0)$ with no prime strictly between $(0)$ and $\mathfrak q$. Let $O\subseteq N$ be the union of $q^{-1}(U)$ and any such neighbourhoods for all those points. Then
$$W=X\setminus q(N\setminus O)$$
is open, contains $U$ and every height-one point of $X$, and $N\times_X W\to W$ is finite etale. There exist a finite etale morphism $H\to X$ and an isomorphism $H\times_X W\cong N\times_X W$ over $W$; in particular $H\times_X U\cong N\times_X U$ over $U$. For every $x\in X\setminus W$, the ambient local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is regular and has Krull dimension at least two [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Neither normality of $C$ nor henselianity of $B$ is assumed, and the conclusion does not identify $H$ with $N$.

source.place: IX Proposition 2.1(i), printed pp.133-134: regular extension subargument made explicit in returned steps 14-15. Stacks pione.tex Tags 0BMA (lemma-local-purity), 0EY7 (lemma-extend-pure); finite closed-image construction of the base open uses lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres. The finite etale extension is a new model, not an asserted identification with the normalization.

proof.text: At each point of O, choose either the inverse image of D(f) or one of the supplied neighbourhoods containing that point. Its structural map to X is etale: for the first case compose the given restriction with the open immersion D(f) → X; the second case is hVet. Once q⁻¹(W) ⊆ O is known, pull these neighbourhoods back along q⁻¹(W) → N. Their maps to X are etale by restriction and composition. The point-indexed neighbourhoods cover q⁻¹(W), so source locality gives etaleness of q⁻¹(W) → X. Cancel the open immersion W → X to obtain etaleness over W.

Let $Z=N\setminus O$. It is closed. Since $q$ is finite, its image $q(Z)$ is closed. Hence $W=X\setminus q(Z)$ is open. For a point $x\in X$, membership $x\in W$ says exactly that every point of the fibre $q^{-1}(\{x\})$ lies in $O$. If $x\in U$, its entire fibre lies in $N_U\subseteq O$, so $U\subseteq W$. This also shows $q^{-1}(W)\subseteq O$.

source.place: Tag 01WN (lemma-finite-proper), used for the closed image of Z.

proof.text: If a height-one prime $\mathfrak q$ does not contain $f$, it belongs to $U\subseteq W$. If $f\in\mathfrak q$, every point $z$ over $\mathfrak q$ belongs to its chosen $O_z\subseteq O$. The fibre criterion of step 2 therefore gives $\mathfrak q\in W$ as well. An empty fibre satisfies the same criterion. Also $(0)\in U$, since $B$ is a domain and $f\ne0$. Thus a prime $\mathfrak p$ outside $W$ is neither zero nor height one: by the stated meaning of height one there is a prime $\mathfrak r$ with $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak r\subsetneq\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), definition of D(f); the height-one condition in the item.

proof.text: For x outside W, height(x) is nonzero: height zero is equivalent to the zero ideal in the domain B, but the zero ideal belongs to D(f) since f is nonzero. Height(x) is not one, since all height-one points belong to W. Thus height(x) ≥ 2 in the extended natural numbers. Mathlib ringKrullDim_stalk_eq_coheight and idealHeight_eq_coheight identify the dimension of the affine stalk with this height. The affine stalk is regular by transporting the regularity of Localization.AtPrime x.asIdeal through Spec.stalkIso. Finally B is Noetherian by IsRegularRing, hence Spec B is locally Noetherian. This replaces the explicit chain-and-contraction calculation by the proved Mathlib height identity.

source.place: Tag 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization), explicit fraction argument; Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves)(6); regularity and dimension definitions Tags 00OD and 00KE.

proof.text: The restriction q|W is finite by base change. Its etaleness is proved by the source-neighbourhood argument in step 1 using the inclusion q⁻¹(W) ⊆ O from step 2, followed by cancellation of W → X. Thus no separate isomorphism between the base changes of O and N is needed.

source.place: Tags 01WL (lemma-base-change-finite), 02GO (lemma-base-change-etale); restriction along an open immersion.

proof.text: Apply the regular codimension-two extension theorem with $L=X$, $V=W$, and the finite etale morphism $q_W$ of step 5. Its base hypothesis is supplied by step 4: $X$ is locally Noetherian, and every missing ambient stalk is regular of dimension at least two. It gives a finite etale $p:H\to X$ and an isomorphism $N\times_XW\cong H\times_XW$ over $W$. Invert this isomorphism to obtain the displayed comparison in the item. The theorem extends the restricted cover; it imposes no normality condition on the original algebra $C$.

source.place: Tags 0BMA (lemma-local-purity)(1) and 0EY7 (lemma-extend-pure), as packaged by the cited existing extension theorem.

proof.text: Use pullbackRestrictIsoRestrict to convert the extension theorem comparison into ew : H ×X W ≅ N ×X W, compatible with the second projections. Put i : D(f) → W. Pull back ew using pullback.map with identity maps on D(f) and W; it is an isomorphism because ew is. On both sides use pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso and pullback.congrHom for i ≫ W.ι = D(f).ι. Compose these three isomorphisms. The pullback projection identities give the required compatibility over D(f).
